About Beyond Klean

What is Beyond Klean?

Beyond Klean is a specialty cleaning procurement platform for construction and commercial buildings. We help builders and owners define the cleaning scope and connect them with independent, verified contractors who quote and perform the work.

Does Beyond Klean do the cleaning itself?

No. Independent, verified contractors perform the work. Beyond Klean handles scoping, matching, coordination and documentation, and the contractor that quotes the job performs, insures and warrants it.

How is Beyond Klean different from a lead-selling directory?

We do not sell your request to a list of companies. Each request is scoped and qualified, then matched to contractors verified for that specific work, with capacity confirmed before an introduction.

What areas does Beyond Klean serve?

The service library is national. Contractor coverage is being built market by market, starting in Florida, and we tell you plainly whether a verified contractor covers your location.

What kinds of buildings does Beyond Klean cover?

Commercial, retail, grocery, restaurant, warehouse, industrial, office, healthcare, education, hospitality and multifamily projects, from tenant improvements to ground-up construction.

How many cleaning services does Beyond Klean list?

438 distinct services across 20 service families, searchable under nearly a thousand names that contractors, specs and buyers use for them.

Is there a cost to request a quote?

No. Requesting a scope review and quote is free for project owners and general contractors.

What is the relationship with Above Eye Level Cleaning?

Above Eye Level Cleaning is our partner program for recurring overhead and high-dusting work. Beyond Klean covers construction turnover, and AELC keeps overhead surfaces clean after the building opens.

For general contractors

How do I get a cleaning sub for my project?

Request a quote or send your bid package. We review the scope, phases, schedule and site details, then introduce a verified contractor who prices the work directly with you.

Can you price from my drawings and specs?

Yes. Send drawings, the Division 01 cleaning section and any finish schedules. The matched contractor prices the scope; we help make sure nothing is missing, such as overhead cleaning or glass.

Can one request cover rough, final and touch-up cleaning?

Yes. Most construction cleaning is bid by phase. One request can cover every phase, with each priced separately.

What if I need a cleaning crew tomorrow?

Tell us the deadline. We only promise a response after a contractor confirms capacity, and we will tell you plainly if we cannot cover it in time.

Do your contractors carry insurance?

Contractors must provide current insurance certificates before they are routed work, and expired documents pause routing automatically. Project-specific requirements such as additional insured status are confirmed by the contractor.

Who do I pay?

You contract with and pay the cleaning contractor that performs the work, under the terms you agree with them.

Can you help with multi-site rollouts?

Yes. National and regional programs can use one scope and checklist across many sites, with local verified contractors where coverage exists.

What documentation do I get at closeout?

Contractors can provide photo documentation, room checklists and product data sheets for the cleaners used, which help with closeout packages and LEED or IAQ requirements.

For owners and facility managers

When should cleaning be planned on a construction project?

Early. Overhead cleaning, glass, floors and kitchen equipment are often missed in scopes. Writing them in during bidding prevents change orders at the end.

Why is my new building still dusty after the final clean?

Usually because overhead surfaces were not in scope, or dust was moved instead of captured. HEPA capture and overhead cleaning fix the cause, not just the symptom.

Can Beyond Klean help after we open?

Yes. Recurring overhead and high dusting goes through Above Eye Level Cleaning, and floor, glass and specialty services can be arranged as needed.

Is construction cleaning the same as janitorial service?

No. Construction cleaning removes construction residue from new finishes: dust, labels, adhesive, grout haze and debris. Janitorial service maintains an occupied building.

How do I know the cleaning was done right?

Ask for room checklists and before-and-after photos, and walk the space with the punch list. We track complaints so performance is visible.

Can cleaning be scheduled around our operations?

Yes. Remodels in operating stores, offices and healthcare facilities are commonly cleaned overnight or in phases.

What should I check at the owner walk?

Look up at ceilings and fixtures, open drawers, check glass in daylight, look behind toilets and under sinks, and check floor edges and corners.

Who is responsible if something is damaged during cleaning?

The contractor performing the work is responsible under its contract and insurance. That is one reason we verify insurance before routing.

For cleaning contractors

How do I join the Beyond Klean network?

Apply through the Join the Network page with your company details, services, coverage area, insurance and references. We verify before any project is routed.

Does Beyond Klean sell leads?

No. Requests are scoped and matched to verified contractors with capacity, not sold to a list.

What are the network tiers?

Applicant, verified generalist, verified specialist and conditional specialist. Your tier determines which scopes are routed to you.

Do I set my own prices?

Yes. The executing contractor prices and approves every proposal. Beyond Klean does not set your price.

Can specialty contractors join?

Yes. Floor care, glass, high dusting, kitchen, pressure washing and other specialists are needed, and regulated specialties are reviewed case by case.

What documents are required?

Legal business information, insurance certificates, relevant licenses, safety program information, references and your service area and capacity.

Is there a cost to join?

Commercial terms are discussed during onboarding and agreed in writing before any work is routed.

Can I serve only part of a state?

Yes. You set your service area and the scopes you want, and routing follows them.

Green and safer cleaning

What makes Beyond Klean's approach greener?

Methods first: capture dust with HEPA instead of blowing it around, use microfiber and water before chemicals, pick pH-neutral and low-VOC products matched to the surface, and recover wash water instead of sending it to storm drains.

Do you use non-toxic cleaning products?

We avoid blanket claims like non-toxic. We describe the specific methods and products used and provide their data sheets, because every product has handling requirements.

What is capture-first cleaning?

Removing dust and soil from the building, with HEPA vacuums and microfiber, instead of moving it into the air or onto other surfaces.

Why does least-aggressive chemistry matter on new buildings?

New finishes are at their most vulnerable. Harsh acids and solvents can etch stone, dull coatings, damage grout and void warranties.

Are green cleaning products less effective?

Not when they are matched to the job. Many construction residues come off with mechanical methods and neutral products; stronger chemistry is reserved for when it is truly needed.

Do you follow green building requirements?

Contractors can follow project IAQ plans, document products and methods, and support LEED documentation for cleaning-related credits.

What certifications matter for green cleaning?

EPA Safer Choice certifies products, and Green Seal GS-42 certifies cleaning service providers. Project specs may name others.

How is wash water handled?

Exterior washing uses recovery equipment or drain protection so dirty water does not enter storm drains.

Pricing and scheduling

How is construction cleaning priced?

By square foot, by phase, by crew-day or by line item, depending on scope. Overhead work, glass and floor care are often priced separately.

What affects the price most?

Square footage, ceiling height and access, number of phases, finish types, the amount of residue, schedule pressure and night or weekend work.

Why do you not publish prices?

Prices depend on local labor, access and scope. We provide pricing factors, and the contractor prices after reviewing the actual project.

How far in advance should cleaning be booked?

As early as the bid phase. Final cleaning is scheduled around inspection dates, and crews book up near quarter-end and holiday openings.

Is night work more expensive?

Usually, because of labor premiums. It is often worth it for operating stores and occupied buildings.

Are re-cleans extra?

That depends on the contract. Clear re-clean terms in the scope avoid disputes at the end of the job.

How long does a final clean take?

From one day for a small tenant space to several weeks for large buildings cleaned in phases.

Can cleaning be split between phases of occupancy?

Yes. Each area can be final-cleaned and protected as it is handed over.

Site, Debris & Waste Management

Who is responsible for jobsite debris on a commercial project?

The general contractor is responsible overall, and most subcontracts make each trade clean up its own waste. In practice trades leave scraps behind, so GCs often hire a dedicated cleanup crew to sweep, haul and sort daily or weekly.

How often should a construction site be cleaned?

Busy interiors usually need a daily sweep of walking paths and a deeper weekly clean. Fast-track jobs with many trades on site sometimes need two passes a day near egress routes and stairwells.

What is the difference between debris removal and a rough clean?

Debris removal is ongoing: it clears waste as it is created. A rough clean is a defined phase after framing, drywall and rough-in that removes bulk debris and dust so finish trades can start.

Can construction waste be recycled?

Yes. Metal, clean wood, cardboard and gypsum drywall are commonly recycled where local haulers accept them. Separating streams at the source usually lowers haul costs and supports LEED waste-diversion credits.

Does Beyond Klean provide dumpsters?

No. The roll-off is usually arranged by the GC or the hauler. The cleanup contractors we match load, sort and manage the debris that goes into them.

What does OSHA require for jobsite housekeeping?

OSHA's construction rules require walking and working surfaces to be kept free of scrap, debris and protruding nails, and combustible waste to be removed regularly. Where silica dust is present, dry sweeping is restricted in favor of wet or HEPA methods.

Can a cleanup crew work while other trades are on site?

Yes, and most progress cleaning happens exactly that way. Crews coordinate with the superintendent's look-ahead schedule so they clear areas between trades without blocking work.

How is jobsite cleanup priced?

It is usually priced per visit, per crew-day or as a monthly allowance, based on square footage, number of floors, debris volume and whether hauling is included. Contractors confirm pricing after reviewing the site and schedule.

How often should debris be removed from each floor?

On active floors, usually daily or every other day. Slower areas may need only a weekly sweep. The superintendent's schedule drives it.

Rough Clean

When does the rough clean happen?

After framing, drywall hanging and taping, and mechanical, electrical and plumbing rough-in are complete, and before flooring, ceilings and finish carpentry start. On large buildings it moves floor by floor.

What is included in a rough clean?

Removing bulk debris, scraping drywall mud and overspray off slabs, vacuuming stud bays and openings, and clearing mechanical rooms and shafts. Fine detailing waits for the final clean.

Why not skip the rough clean and do one big final clean?

Dust and debris left at rough stage get trapped behind ceilings, inside ductwork and under new flooring. A rough clean protects finishes and makes the final clean faster and cheaper.

Is a rough clean the same as a construction clean?

It is one phase of it. Construction cleaning usually runs in three phases: rough clean, light or detail clean, and final clean, with touch-up before the owner walk.

How long does a rough clean take?

It depends on square footage, debris volume and access. A small tenant space may take a day; a multistory building is usually phased over several days as floors become ready.

Should the slab be scraped before flooring is installed?

Yes. Hardened joint compound, paint drips and overspray under resilient flooring or carpet create bumps and adhesion problems. Flooring installers expect a clean, scraped slab.

Who sets the rough clean schedule?

The general contractor's superintendent, based on when each area is released by the drywall and MEP trades. Good cleanup contractors work from the GC's three-week look-ahead.

Does a rough clean require HEPA equipment?

On most commercial jobs it should. Drywall and concrete dust are fine enough to pass through ordinary vacuums, and silica rules restrict dry sweeping where concrete dust is present.

What does a rough clean include?

Bulk debris removal, slab scraping, HEPA vacuuming of floors, sills and openings, and clearing mechanical rooms and shafts.

Fine Dust, Drywall Dust & Controlled-Dust Cleaning

Why does drywall dust keep coming back after cleaning?

Because it was moved, not removed. Dry dusting and sweeping lift fine particles into the air, where they settle again hours later. HEPA vacuuming and damp microfiber capture it so it stays gone.

Is drywall dust harmful?

Drywall dust can irritate eyes, skin and lungs, and some joint compounds contain crystalline silica. Concrete and masonry dust carry more silica. Capture methods and proper respiratory protection reduce exposure.

What is HEPA vacuuming?

Vacuuming with a sealed machine whose high-efficiency particulate air filter captures at least 99.97 percent of particles at 0.3 microns. It keeps fine construction dust from passing straight through the vacuum back into the room.

Can you use a leaf blower or compressed air to clean construction dust?

It is a poor practice indoors and restricted under OSHA's silica standard. Blowing dust spreads it into finished spaces and HVAC systems and increases worker exposure.

How is dust controlled during renovation of an occupied building?

With containment barriers, negative air machines, sticky mats at exits, HEPA vacuuming and frequent damp cleaning outside the work zone. Healthcare projects follow stricter infection-control protocols.

When should fine dust removal happen?

Last, after all dust-producing trades are finished in that area. Dusting before ceiling, electrical or millwork touch-ups finish usually means doing it twice.

Does fine dust removal include inside cabinets and drawers?

It should. Owners and inspectors open drawers and cabinet doors, and dust collects inside them during construction. Confirm it is in the scope.

What is silica-aware housekeeping?

Cleaning methods that keep crystalline silica dust out of the air: wet sweeping, HEPA vacuuming and approved sweeping compounds instead of dry sweeping, brushing or compressed air.

Why does drywall dust keep showing up after cleaning?

It was moved instead of captured. HEPA vacuuming and damp microfiber remove it; dry dusting puts it back in the air.

Fine drywall dust removal from all horizontal surfaces →

What is the best way to remove drywall dust?

HEPA vacuum first, then wipe with damp microfiber, working top to bottom.

Overhead & Elevated Surfaces (Above Eye Level)

What is high dusting?

Cleaning surfaces that are out of normal reach, usually above eight to ten feet: open ceiling decks, beams, joists, ductwork, pipes, cable trays, light fixtures and the tops of racking and walls.

Why do new buildings need overhead cleaning?

Construction dust rises and settles on every horizontal surface overhead. In open-ceiling stores, warehouses and restaurants it is visible, falls onto finished surfaces and can fail food-safety and owner inspections.

How do crews clean ceilings 20 or 30 feet up?

With scissor lifts or boom lifts, extension poles and HEPA vacuum attachments that capture dust at the surface. Dust should be captured, not knocked down onto the floor.

Is overhead cleaning included in a normal final clean?

Often it is not. Many final-clean scopes stop at reachable surfaces. If the building has an open ceiling or exposed structure, overhead cleaning should be written into the bid as its own line item.

How often should high dusting be done after the building opens?

Retail and warehouse spaces typically schedule it quarterly or semiannually. Food facilities often tie it to audit schedules. Heavy-dust environments may need it more often.

Can high dusting be done while a store is open?

Yes, usually overnight or before opening, with merchandise covered or areas cordoned off. Lift work over shoppers is avoided.

Is high dusting safe for sprinkler heads?

Sprinkler heads need careful, light dusting only. Crews should never hang anything from them, paint them or use pressure on them. Damaged or painted heads must be replaced by a fire protection contractor.

What is Above Eye Level Cleaning?

Our partner program focused on overhead cleaning. Beyond Klean handles construction turnover; AboveEyeLevelCleaning.com handles the scheduled high dusting that keeps the space clean after it opens.

How do you clean an exposed metal deck without making a mess below?

Capture the dust where it sits. Crews use HEPA vacuums with brush heads on extension poles from a lift and cover finished surfaces below. Dry brushing or blowing simply moves the dust to the floor and fixtures.

Open ceiling deck cleaning →

Is it worth cleaning a painted deck that looks clean from the floor?

Usually yes. Dust that is invisible from 25 feet still falls as fixtures vibrate and HVAC cycles. Retail and food tenants often find it on product within weeks if the deck is skipped.

Open ceiling deck cleaning →

When should the deck be cleaned in the construction sequence?

After all overhead trades, including sprinkler, electrical and HVAC balancing, are done above that area, and before the final floor clean. Cleaning before the last overhead trade leaves usually means paying twice.

Open ceiling deck cleaning →

Can the deck be cleaned in sections while other work continues?

Yes. Large buildings are typically cleaned in bays or column lines that match the lift plan, so other trades can keep working in areas that are not under the lift.

Walls, Ceilings & Interior Finishes

Can you wash freshly painted walls?

Not right away. Most latex paints need days to weeks to cure fully, depending on the product. Early cleaning should be light spot cleaning with neutral cleaners and soft microfiber, not scrubbing.

How do you clean acoustic ceiling tiles without staining them?

With dry methods first: dry sponges, soft brushes and HEPA vacuuming. Liquid cleaners can leave water rings on mineral fiber tile. Badly soiled tiles are often cheaper to replace.

Who cleans the ceiling grid after construction?

It should be in the cleaning contractor's final clean scope. Grid gets fingerprints from tile setters and dust from above-ceiling work, and it is a common punch item.

Should air diffusers be cleaned before turnover?

Yes. Diffusers and return grilles catch construction dust and often show dark streaks soon after the HVAC starts. Face cleaning is part of final clean; duct interior cleaning is a separate specialty.

What is the best way to remove scuffs from walls?

Start with the gentlest option: a damp microfiber cloth, then a neutral cleaner, then a melamine sponge used lightly. Aggressive rubbing burnishes flat paint and leaves a shiny patch.

Do wallcoverings need special cleaning?

Yes. Vinyl wallcovering tolerates mild cleaners; fabric and natural-fiber wallcoverings need dry methods. Always follow the manufacturer's care instructions.

Are wall and ceiling smudges really punch-list items?

Yes. Architects and owners routinely list fingerprints, overspray and smudges on walls and ceilings during the punch walk.

What about walls above 10 feet?

Upper walls, ledges and soffits need lifts or poles and are usually part of the overhead scope. They collect dust the same way decks and ducts do.

How do you clean scuffs off new paint without damaging it?

Gently, starting with water and microfiber, then a neutral cleaner, testing in an inconspicuous spot.

Why does cleaning leave shiny spots on walls?

Rubbing flat or matte paint burnishes it. Use light pressure and the gentlest method.

Doors, Hardware, Millwork & Casework

Should the labels on fire-rated doors be removed?

No. The fire rating label on the door edge and frame must stay in place and readable. Cleaners should work around it and never paint over or remove it.

How do you clean new cabinets after construction?

Vacuum dust from inside boxes and drawers, then wipe with a mild cleaner suitable for the finish. Avoid ammonia, abrasive pads and excess water, which can damage wood finishes and edge banding.

What cleaner is safe for quartz countertops?

Mild, pH-neutral cleaners and soft cloths. Strong alkalis, solvents and abrasive pads can dull or discolor the resin in engineered quartz.

How should brass and stainless door hardware be cleaned?

With a soft cloth and a cleaner made for that finish. Abrasives scratch, and some metal polishes strip protective lacquer from brass and bronze.

Do toilet partitions need special cleaning?

Powder-coated, plastic laminate, solid plastic and stainless partitions each have recommended cleaners. Most need only a neutral cleaner; sticker and adhesive removal needs care on powder coat.

Is cleaning inside drawers part of a final clean?

On a well-written scope, yes. Inspectors and owners open them, and they collect construction dust and packaging debris.

What is the most common millwork punch item?

Dust, adhesive and pencil marks on cabinet faces and inside boxes, followed by fingerprints and protective film left on edges and hardware.

Who removes the blue protective film on new hardware and appliances?

Usually the cleaning crew at final clean, unless the installer is required to. Film left too long in sun or heat becomes hard to remove.

How should new wood doors be cleaned after construction?

With mild, wood-safe cleaners and soft cloths, removing labels carefully so the factory finish is not damaged.

Glass, Windows & Glazing

Why does new glass get scratched during construction cleaning?

Scratches come from dragging debris under a blade, from fabricating debris fused to tempered glass, and from using dull or dirty scrapers. Proper lubrication, fresh blades and the right technique on the right glass type reduce the risk.

Can razor blades be used on new windows?

On uncoated glass, a clean blade used flat with lubrication is a standard method. Some coated, tempered and low-E surfaces should not be scraped at all. The glass manufacturer's guidance controls.

What is a glass scratch waiver?

A contract clause, recommended by the window cleaning industry, that addresses liability for scratches that may result from removing construction debris from glass. Many construction window cleaners require one.

When should construction windows be cleaned?

After exterior finishes like stucco, painting and sealants are complete and the scaffolding is down, then touched up after punch work. Cleaning earlier usually means cleaning twice.

How do you remove concrete splatter from glass?

Carefully, starting with soaking and gentle mechanical removal. Acidic concrete removers can etch glass and damage metal frames, so they are a last resort and must be tested first.

Who cleans high-rise windows after construction?

Specialty contractors using rope access, swing stages or building maintenance units. It requires trained, insured crews and fall-protection plans, so it is routed only to qualified providers.

What is pure-water window cleaning?

Cleaning with deionized or reverse-osmosis water through a water-fed pole. With minerals removed, glass dries without spots, and little or no detergent is needed.

Should the stickers on new windows be removed?

Yes, at final clean, unless the inspector needs to see energy labels first. Ask the GC whether the code inspection requires labels in place.

When should interior windows be cleaned on a construction project?

Near the end, after painting, caulking and window treatment installation are complete, and right before the owner walk.

Usually, but it should be listed in the scope with sills, frames and tracks so nothing is missed.

Does new VCT need to be stripped before waxing?

New VCT has a factory coating that must be removed or prepared before floor finish will bond. That is why new VCT gets an initial scrub or strip and multiple coats of finish, not just a mop and wax.

How is a new concrete floor cleaned?

Usually with an auto-scrubber, a neutral or mildly alkaline cleaner and pads chosen for the finish. Polished and sealed concrete need gentler pads and cleaners than raw slabs.

What is efflorescence?

A white, powdery salt deposit that appears when water moves through concrete, masonry or grout and evaporates. It needs a remover matched to the surface, and the moisture source should be found.

Is polishing concrete part of cleaning?

No. Concrete grinding and polishing is a flooring specialty with heavy equipment and silica controls. Cleaning contractors maintain polished concrete; polishing contractors create it.

How long before new floors can be cleaned?

Tile grout, floor finishes, epoxy and wood coatings each have cure times. Cleaning too early can damage them. The installer's cure schedule should be in the cleaning plan.

Who removes tire and forklift marks from new warehouse floors?

The cleaning contractor at final clean, using scrubbers with appropriate pads and cleaners. Non-marking tires on lifts reduce the problem.

What is an auto-scrubber?

A walk-behind or ride-on floor machine that lays down cleaning solution, scrubs with pads or brushes and vacuums the dirty water back up in a single pass.

It depends on the finish: more aggressive pads or brushes for raw slabs, softer pads for sealed or polished concrete to avoid scratching.

Carpet & Soft Surfaces

Does new carpet need to be cleaned before move-in?

Yes. Even when carpet is installed late, it collects drywall dust, footprints and debris during punch and furniture installation. A thorough HEPA vacuum is the minimum; extraction is common.

Can drywall mud be removed from carpet?

Usually, if it is handled properly. Let it dry, break it up and vacuum it, then treat the remaining residue. Wiping wet mud spreads it into the fibers.

How long does carpet take to dry after extraction?

Usually a few hours with low-moisture methods and good airflow. Over-wetting can cause odors, delamination and wicking stains.

What causes stains to reappear after carpet cleaning?

Wicking. Soil or residue deep in the backing rises back to the fiber tips as the carpet dries. Proper extraction and rinsing reduce it.

Should carpet tile be cleaned differently than broadloom?

Similar methods apply, but carpet tile can be lifted and replaced, so badly damaged tiles are often swapped rather than cleaned.

Do construction cleaners clean office furniture?

Many do vacuuming and wipe-down after furniture installation. Upholstery extraction is usually a separate line item.

What vacuum should be used on new carpet?

A commercial HEPA-filtered upright or backpack vacuum. Ordinary filters pass fine drywall dust back into the air.

Is carpet protection film safe to leave on?

Only for a short time. Adhesive film left too long, especially in heat or sun, can leave residue and damage pile.

Why does new carpet look dusty after vacuuming?

Fine drywall dust needs slow, repeated passes with a HEPA vacuum. A single fast pass leaves much of it in the pile.

Construction carpet vacuuming →

What kind of vacuum is best for construction dust in carpet?

A commercial upright or backpack with sealed HEPA filtration, so fine dust is captured instead of exhausted.

Restrooms & Plumbing Fixtures

How do you remove stickers from new toilets and sinks?

Peel the label, then remove the adhesive with a product that is safe for vitreous china and chrome. Razor blades can scratch glazes and plated finishes.

Can acidic bowl cleaners be used on new restroom fixtures?

They should be avoided at turnover. New chrome, grout and some stone are sensitive to acids. Neutral cleaners and non-acidic descalers are safer for initial cleaning.

What is caulk haze?

A thin film of silicone or sealant left on surfaces around a joint after caulking. It attracts dirt and looks smeary. It needs a remover that will not damage the surrounding finish.

Should restroom cleaning include floor drains?

Yes. Floor drains often collect grout, debris and mortar during construction and should be checked and cleaned so they drain freely at turnover.

Who cleans the restroom accessories?

The cleaning contractor during final clean: soap and towel dispensers, grab bars, mirrors, hand dryers and partitions.

Is disinfecting part of a construction restroom clean?

Cleaning is. Disinfecting is a separate step that requires EPA-registered products used according to the label, and it is only claimed when actually done that way.

How clean does a restroom need to be for the owner walk?

Free of dust, labels, residue, smears and debris, with fixtures polished and drains clear. Inspectors look under sinks, behind toilets and inside stalls.

Do eyewash stations need cleaning before turnover?

The exterior should be cleaned. Flushing and testing is the facility's responsibility under its safety program.

How are new toilets and urinals cleaned after construction?

Labels and residue are removed, then fixtures are cleaned inside and out with non-acidic products safe for vitreous china and chrome, including bases, bolt caps and flush valves.

Kitchens, Food Facilities & FRP

What is FRP?

Fiberglass reinforced plastic: the washable, textured wall panels used in commercial kitchens, restrooms and food areas. It is installed with adhesive and trim, and it needs non-abrasive cleaning.

Who cleans a new restaurant before opening?

A post-construction cleaning contractor handles the building and equipment exteriors. Hood and duct cleaning, ice machine sanitizing and refrigeration startup are usually done by their own specialty contractors.

Is kitchen hood cleaning part of construction cleaning?

The hood exterior is. Hood and grease duct interior cleaning is a regulated specialty under NFPA 96 and is done by certified hood cleaning contractors.

What is the difference between cleaning and sanitizing a food surface?

Cleaning removes soil and residue. Sanitizing reduces microorganisms to safe levels and must be done with registered sanitizers at label concentrations. Food-contact surfaces need both, in that order.

How do you remove construction dust from a walk-in cooler?

Vacuum and wipe panels, shelving and floors with food-safe cleaners before the box is started up and stocked. Dust in a running cooler can end up on product.

What do health inspectors look for at a new restaurant opening?

Clean, intact, cleanable surfaces; no construction debris; working handwash sinks; clean equipment; and no dust over food areas. Overhead dust is a common finding.

Can grocery departments open in phases?

Yes. Grocery openings often turn over by department, and cleaning must follow each department's handover date, especially deli, bakery and meat rooms.

Why is stainless steel streaky after cleaning?

Streaks come from residue, hard water or wiping against the grain. Clean with a neutral cleaner, rinse, dry and finish with the grain.

What does a restaurant post-construction clean include?

Ceilings, hood exteriors, walls, equipment exteriors, food-contact surfaces, floors, drains and restrooms, cleaned top down with food-safe products.

Mechanical, Electrical & Construction IAQ

Can a cleaning crew clean an electrical room?

Only non-invasive cleaning of floors, walls and enclosure exteriors, and only where the electrical contractor or facility allows it. Nothing inside energized equipment, and no liquids near live gear.

What is construction indoor air quality management?

A plan, often required on LEED projects, to keep dust and contaminants out of the HVAC system and building during construction: protecting ducts, filtering returns, housekeeping and scheduling.

Should HVAC filters be changed before occupancy?

Yes. Filters that ran during construction are loaded with dust. Green building standards call for new filtration media before occupancy.

What is a building flush-out?

Running the HVAC system with outdoor air for a set period after construction, before or during early occupancy, to dilute contaminants from new finishes. A thorough final clean should come first.

Is duct cleaning part of a construction cleanup?

Duct exteriors are. Duct interior cleaning is a specialty, often done to NADCA standards, and is only needed when ducts were contaminated during construction.

Why were the ducts capped during construction?

To keep construction dust out of them. If caps were missed or torn, dust gets in, and duct cleaning may be needed before turnover.

Who cleans the rooftop units?

The exterior of rooftop units and curbs can be cleaned by the cleaning contractor. Coils and internal components belong to the mechanical contractor.

Does Beyond Klean provide IAQ testing?

No. Air quality testing is done by independent industrial hygiene or commissioning professionals. Our network handles the cleaning and documentation that supports it.

What is included in mechanical room cleaning after construction?

Debris removal, HEPA vacuuming and damp wiping of equipment exteriors, piping, walls and floors, plus clearing floor drains, all without touching controls or opening equipment.

Mechanical room cleaning →

Why do commissioning agents care about clean mechanical rooms?

Dust and debris can clog filters, coils and motors during testing, and a clean room makes leaks and labeling problems easy to spot.

Mechanical room cleaning →

Can a cleaning crew wipe down boilers and pumps?

Crews can wipe the cool, de-energized exterior surfaces. Anything inside the equipment, and any energized or hot surface, is left to the mechanical contractor.

Mechanical room cleaning →

Should mechanical room floors be sealed before turnover?

Many specs call for sealed or painted floors in mechanical rooms. Cleaning should be finished before any sealer goes down, and the sealer manufacturer's cleaning guidance followed afterward.

Retail Fixtures & Store Opening

When should the cleaning crew start on a new store?

After fixtures are installed and before merchandise is set. Most store openings need a fixture clean, a merchandise-set support clean and a final pre-opening clean.

What is a store opening clean?

The final clean of a new or remodeled store before it opens: floors, glass, fixtures, fitting rooms, stockrooms and restrooms, timed around merchandise delivery and the opening date.

Can remodels be cleaned overnight while the store stays open?

Yes. Overnight crews clean after each night's construction so the store can trade the next morning. It takes coordination with the remodel schedule.

How do national retailers handle cleaning for many locations?

Through rollout programs: one scope, one checklist and coordinated crews across many sites, so every store opens to the same standard.

Who cleans gondola shelving?

The cleaning contractor, after the fixture installer is done and before stocking. Shelves, uprights, kick plates and price channels all collect dust.

Does store opening cleaning include the ceiling?

It should for open-ceiling stores. Dust from the deck falls onto merchandise and fixtures after opening if it is not cleaned first.

How long does a store opening clean take?

It depends on size and how many trades are still working. A small store may need a day; a big box store may need multiple shifts over several days.

Do restaurant chains use the same approach?

Yes. Chains typically standardize their opening clean across locations and add kitchen-specific items for health inspection.

When should a new store be cleaned before opening?

In stages: overhead cleaning before fixtures go in, fixture cleaning before merchandise is set, and floors, glass and the entrance right before opening day.

Store opening clean →

What is included in a retail store opening clean?

Overhead structure, light fixtures, fixtures and shelving, glass and storefront, fitting rooms, cash wrap, stockroom, restrooms and floors, plus the entrance and sidewalk.

Store opening clean →

How long does a store opening clean take?

From one day for a small shop to several days or overnight shifts for a big-box store, usually split around fixture and merchandise delivery.

Usually the GC, working with the retailer's opening or construction manager so cleaning stays ahead of merchandise.

Specialty & Controlled Environments

Is post-construction cleaning in a hospital different?

Yes. Healthcare construction follows infection-control risk assessments, and final cleaning before patients return is protocol-based, often coordinated with the hospital's environmental services department.

What is cleanroom cleaning?

Cleaning to a defined particle standard using specific garments, low-lint wipes, approved cleaning agents and a set sequence. It is required before cleanroom certification.

Who cleans a data center after construction?

Specialty contractors trained for critical environments. They clean subfloors, raised floor tiles, cabinets and surfaces with antistatic methods and HEPA equipment.

Do schools have special cleaning requirements after construction?

Schools usually open on fixed dates, have many identical rooms and often require background-checked crews. Low-odor products matter because students arrive soon after.

What is a hotel PIP?

A property improvement plan, a brand-required renovation. PIP cleaning turns renovated rooms back to inventory quickly, often floor by floor.

Can any cleaning company clean a lab?

Not safely. Labs may have chemical, biological or equipment hazards. Cleaning is limited to what the lab's safety officer approves.

How are specialty cleaning contractors verified?

By checking training, protocols, references for that facility type, and insurance that covers the work. Regulated scopes are approved case by case.

Are warehouses considered specialty environments?

Not usually, but their size calls for ride-on scrubbers, lifts for racking and high dusting, and crews that work fast across very large slabs.

What is an infection control risk assessment?

A healthcare planning tool that classifies construction work by risk and sets the dust control and cleaning measures required, often called an ICRA.

Healthcare post-construction terminal-style clean →

Who cleans a hospital after construction?

Trained post-construction crews working with the hospital's environmental services department, which usually does or verifies the final terminal clean.

Why is hospital construction cleaning different from office cleaning?

Patients may be highly vulnerable to airborne contaminants, so methods, products and sign-off follow infection control protocols.

No. Healthcare work is routed only to crews trained in healthcare construction protocols, and only after review.

Exterior, Hardscape & Building Envelope

Can wash water from pressure washing go into the storm drain?

Generally no. Wash water often carries soil, concrete fines, oils and detergents that storm water rules prohibit. Crews use recovery equipment or block and vacuum the drains.

How do you clean mortar off new brick?

With a masonry cleaner suited to the brick type, pre-wetting the wall and rinsing thoroughly. The wrong acid can stain light-colored brick or burn mortar joints.

When is the exterior cleaned on a construction project?

After landscaping, striping and exterior trades finish, and before the certificate of occupancy inspection and owner walk.

What is soft washing?

Cleaning facades and roofs with low pressure and cleaning solutions instead of high pressure, which can damage stucco, EIFS, paint and sealants.

Is parking lot sweeping part of a construction cleanup?

Often yes, especially before striping and before the final walk. Power sweepers handle large lots quickly.

Can graffiti be removed from new construction?

Usually, with removers matched to the surface. Fresh graffiti is much easier to remove, and anti-graffiti coatings can protect high-risk walls.

Who cleans the gutters at the end of a project?

The cleaning contractor or roofer. Gutters and roof drains collect construction debris that can cause backups in the first heavy rain.

Should solar panels be cleaned after construction?

If construction dust coated them, yes, but only by crews following the panel manufacturer's guidance and electrical safety rules.

When can new concrete sidewalks be pressure washed?

Once the concrete has cured enough to resist surface damage. Very young concrete can be etched by high pressure, so crews follow the concrete contractor's timing and start with lower pressure and a surface cleaner.

Sidewalk pressure washing →

Can pressure washing water go into the storm drain?

Generally no. Wash water from construction sites carries concrete fines, soil and residue, so crews block inlets and vacuum the water up, or recover it with reclaim equipment, for approved disposal.

Sidewalk pressure washing →

What is a surface cleaner for pressure washing?

A rotating attachment with spinning nozzles under a hood. It cleans flat concrete evenly without the stripes a wand leaves and reduces overspray onto glass and landscaping.

Sidewalk pressure washing →

Is sidewalk cleaning part of the final construction clean?

Usually yes. Entry walks and sidewalks are cleaned before the owner walk and certificate of occupancy inspection, because mud and slurry on walks track straight into the new building.

Why sweep a parking lot before striping?

Striping paint needs a clean, dry surface to bond. Dirt and grit under the paint make new lines flake off within weeks.

How often should a construction parking lot be swept?

During construction, as needed to control track-out, often weekly near completion. A final sweep happens right before striping and again before turnover.

Power sweeping contractors with truck-mounted or ride-on sweepers, coordinated by the GC or the cleaning contractor.

No. Sweeping removes loose dirt and debris; washing removes stains like oil, rust and concrete slurry using water, cleaners and reclaim equipment.

It should be recovered with vacuum reclaim equipment and disposed of where the local authority allows, rather than flowing into storm drains.

Fresh oil stains often come out with degreasers and hot water. Old stains soaked deep into asphalt or concrete may only lighten.

Residue, Stain & Protective-Material Removal

What does least-aggressive-first mean?

Start with the gentlest method that might work: dry removal, then water, then neutral cleaners, then targeted solvents, and test each one in a hidden spot. Stop at the first method that works.

How do you remove paint overspray from new surfaces?

It depends on the surface and paint type. Plastic blades and mild removers work on many hard surfaces; glass may take a blade; textured and porous surfaces need specialty products and testing.

What removes adhesive residue safely?

Citrus or soy-based removers and mineral oils work on many adhesives without harsh solvents. Some substrates, including certain plastics and finishes, react to solvents, so test first.

Why does protective film need to come off promptly?

Heat and UV make film adhesive bond harder over time. Film left on for months can leave residue or pull finish when removed.

Who removes floor protection at the end of a job?

Usually the cleaning contractor during final clean, unless the flooring contractor or GC handles it. The dust trapped under it must be captured, not swept around.

Is grout haze a cleaning or tile problem?

Both. The tile setter is expected to clean grout as it is installed, but light haze is common and is removed at final clean. Heavy haze goes back to the installer.

Can paint drips on concrete be removed?

Usually, by scraping and with removers suited to the paint and the floor finish. Polished concrete needs gentler methods than raw slab.

What is the most common residue on construction punch lists?

Labels and stickers, paint overspray, tape residue and caulk smears appear on nearly every punch list.

How do you remove paint overspray from windows?

On suitable glass, with a sharp, lubricated blade held flat and fresh water, after confirming the glass type allows scraping.

Paint overspray removal →

How do you know if a surface has overspray?

Run a clean hand or a plastic bag over it or look in raking light. Overspray feels gritty and shows as a dull haze.

Paint overspray removal →

Who is responsible for paint overspray?

Usually the painting contractor under their protection obligations, though GCs often have the cleaning crew remove it and back-charge.

Can overspray be removed from car finishes in a parking area?

Painter's tape is designed for short use. Left on for weeks, especially in sun or heat, its adhesive bonds to the surface and stays behind when the tape is removed.

Vertical Transportation & Circulation

Who cleans the elevator pit?

Pits collect debris during construction and must be clean for inspection. The cleaning contractor can remove debris only with the elevator contractor's lockout and permission.

Why do elevator sills need cleaning?

Debris in sill tracks can keep doors from closing properly and cause service calls. Sills should be vacuumed clean before turnover.

When is the elevator cab protection removed?

Near the end of the project, after heavy deliveries and furniture moves are complete. The cab is then detailed.

How are stairwells cleaned after construction?

Top to bottom: dust rails and ledges, clean treads and nosings, then floors, so dust does not fall onto cleaned areas.

Are escalators cleaned by the cleaning contractor?

Only exterior surfaces and only with the escalator contractor's permission and lockout. Comb plates and step cleaning are specialty work.

What does a lobby final clean include?

Floors, entry glass, walls, signage, furniture, elevator lobbies and any feature walls or lighting. It is the most visible space in the building.

Should stair nosings be cleaned separately?

They need attention because they collect grime and adhesive residue. Nosings are often a visible punch item.

Can corridors be cleaned while tenants move in?

Yes, with phased cleaning that follows move-in schedules and focuses on high-traffic routes.

How are elevator cabs cleaned after construction?

With the cab on independent service, crews clean ceiling, lights, walls, rails, control panel and floor using products matched to each finish.

Can cleaning crews operate elevators?

No. The elevator contractor or building staff places the cab on independent service for cleaning.

Turnover, Punch & Closeout Support

What is the difference between a final clean and a touch-up clean?

The final clean is a complete, detailed clean of the space before inspection. A touch-up clean is a quick pass right before the owner walk, or after punch work, to fix areas that got dirty again.

What does Substantial Completion have to do with cleaning?

Most construction specs require final cleaning to be complete before the GC requests the Substantial Completion inspection. A dirty building can fail that walk and delay the certificate and payment.

What is a sparkle clean?

An informal name for the last detailed touch-up before an owner walk or grand opening. It focuses on glass, fixtures, floors and anything visible.

How many phases does construction cleaning have?

Usually three: rough clean, light or detail clean, and final clean, followed by touch-ups. Not every project needs every phase.

Who pays for re-cleaning after punch work?

That depends on the contract. Many GCs carry a re-clean allowance, or back-charge the trade that made the mess. Cleaning contracts should define how re-cleans are priced.

What cleaning documentation do GCs need for closeout?

Often photo documentation, signed room checklists, product data sheets for cleaning chemicals and records supporting LEED or IAQ requirements.

What is attic stock?

Spare materials left for the owner, such as extra tiles, ceiling panels and paint. It should be cleaned, labeled and staged where the owner wants it.

Can a building be cleaned and turned over in phases?

Yes. Phased occupancy is common in large projects; each area is final-cleaned and protected when it is handed over.

What is included in a final construction clean?

Every surface in every room: overhead, lights, walls, doors, glass, casework, fixtures, restrooms, floors, plus exterior entries and walks.

Final clean of entire building →

When should the final clean happen?

After all trades finish, before the Substantial Completion inspection and owner walk.

Final clean of entire building →

How much does a final clean cost?

It is usually priced per square foot or by crew-day, based on size, finishes, heights and schedule.

Final clean of entire building →

What is the difference between final clean and touch-up?

The final clean is complete and detailed; touch-up is a quick pass to fix areas that got dirty again.

Final clean of entire building →

What else is final clean of entire building called?

Final clean of entire building →

Why do a final clean in phases instead of all at once?

Large buildings and phased occupancies finish one area at a time. Cleaning each area as it is released lets it be inspected, handed over or occupied without waiting for the whole building.

How is a finished phase kept clean while work continues next door?

With floor protection, closed doors or barriers, walk-off mats and controlled access, plus a scheduled touch-up right before handover.

Often somewhat more, because crews mobilize several times and some touch-up is repeated. It is usually offset by earlier occupancy and fewer delays.

The GC and owner set them based on the occupancy plan, inspections and the construction schedule.

No. Small projects often skip it and go from rough clean to final clean. Larger projects use it to keep finishes protected and make the final clean faster.

Surfaces, cabinets, fixtures, window frames and glass get a first detail pass. Floors are often still protected, and final detailing waits for the last phase.

Multifamily & Residential-Scale Turnover

How long does it take to clean a new apartment unit?

A typical unit final clean takes a few crew-hours, depending on size, finishes and how much construction dust is left. Consistent checklists keep units uniform.

Are appliances cleaned inside and out?

They should be: remove packaging, film and labels, then clean interiors and exteriors so the unit is ready to show.

Who cleans amenity spaces in a new apartment community?

The same cleaning contractor, usually before leasing tours start. Clubhouses, fitness rooms and pool areas are prioritized because they sell the property.

What is a model unit clean?

A detailed clean of the units used for tours, often repeated as they get foot traffic during lease-up.

Do units need re-cleaning before move-in?

Often yes, if units sat empty after final clean. A light dust and floor clean before move-in keeps the first impression right.

Can dryer vents be clogged from construction?

Yes. Drywall dust and debris can enter vent lines during construction, and a quick check before turnover can prevent fire risk and complaints.

Do trash rooms and chutes need cleaning at turnover?

Yes. They collect construction debris and odors, and chute doors and rooms should be clean before residents move in.

What is the biggest multifamily cleaning challenge?

Schedule. Units are released on a rolling basis, and cleaning has to match the pace of inspections and lease-up.

What is included in an apartment final clean?

Every surface in the unit: kitchen, appliances inside and out, bathrooms, closets, windows and blinds, fixtures, outlets, baseboards and floors. Crews follow a unit checklist so every unit matches.

Restoration & Regulated Work (Conditional)

Can a regular cleaning company remove mold?

Small, surface-level mold cleanup may be allowed in some places, but remediation of larger areas typically involves licensed or certified professionals, containment and clearance testing, depending on state rules.

Who handles asbestos found during construction?

Work must stop in the area, and a licensed asbestos abatement contractor handles removal under federal and state rules. Cleaning crews must not disturb suspect materials.

What happens if lead paint is disturbed during renovation?

Lead-safe work practices and cleanup are required under EPA and OSHA rules, and clearance testing may be needed. Certified renovators and abatement contractors handle this.

What is post-storm cleanup?

Removing debris, water, mud and damaged materials after hurricanes, floods or wind events, often followed by drying and mold prevention. Florida projects plan for it.

Can construction cleaners disinfect?

Only with EPA-registered disinfectants used according to the label, and only when the claim is accurate. Cleaning and disinfecting are different services.

How does Beyond Klean handle regulated scopes?

They are never routed automatically. Each request is reviewed, and only providers with the required licenses, training and insurance are introduced.

What is a biohazard on a jobsite?

Blood, bodily fluids, sharps or animal waste. Cleanup requires trained personnel, protective equipment and proper disposal.

Is fire and smoke damage cleaning a restoration job?

Yes. Smoke residue cleaning, odor control and contents cleaning are restoration specialties, often handled through insurance claims.

What should be done first after water damage on a jobsite?

Stop the water source, make the area electrically safe and photograph the damage. Then get a qualified restoration contractor drying the structure quickly, because wet materials start growing mold within days.

Water damage cleanup →

How quickly can mold grow after water damage?

Mold can begin growing on wet drywall, wood and insulation within roughly 24 to 48 hours in warm conditions. That is why fast extraction and monitored drying matter so much.

Water damage cleanup →

Who handles water damage restoration on a construction project?

A restoration contractor trained in water damage drying. They extract water, set dehumidifiers and air movers, and track moisture readings until materials are dry.

Water damage cleanup →

Does water damage on a new building need insurance documentation?

Usually yes. Photos, moisture readings and drying logs support builder's risk or property insurance claims and protect the owner's warranty position.

Water damage cleanup →

What else is water damage cleanup called?

Contractors, specs and buyers also call it "flood cleanup". On Beyond Klean, all of these names point to the same scope, so a request under any of them reaches the same qualified contractors.

Water damage cleanup →

Can a regular cleaning company remove mold?

Very small surface spots may be cleaned in some situations, but anything larger should go to a qualified remediation contractor. Disturbing mold without containment spreads spores through the building.

Mold remediation →

Does Florida license mold remediation?

Yes. Florida licenses mold assessors and mold remediators under state law, with limited exemptions, so remediation there should be done by a properly licensed provider.

Mold remediation →

What is clearance testing after mold remediation?

An independent assessment after remediation to confirm the area is acceptable before reconstruction or occupancy. It is often required by owners, lenders or insurers.

Mold remediation →

Why must the moisture source be fixed before mold remediation?

Mold needs moisture to grow. If the leak or humidity problem continues, mold comes back no matter how well the area was cleaned.

Mold remediation →

What else is mold remediation called?

Contractors, specs and buyers also call it "mold removal". On Beyond Klean, all of these names point to the same scope, so a request under any of them reaches the same qualified contractors.

Mold remediation →

Who cleans up after a fire in a building?

Fire restoration contractors trained to identify soot types and use the right removal and deodorizing methods. Cleaning crews without that training can make stains permanent.

Fire and smoke residue cleaning →

Is soot harmful to people?

Soot contains fine particles and combustion byproducts that can irritate lungs and skin. Cleanup crews use respiratory protection and containment.

Fire and smoke residue cleaning →

Can smoke odor be removed completely?

Usually, when residue is removed and odor is treated at the source, including HVAC systems. Odor that persists often means residue was missed.

Fire and smoke residue cleaning →

Is fire restoration covered by insurance?

Often, under builder's risk or property insurance. Restoration contractors typically document the work for the adjuster.

Fire and smoke residue cleaning →

What should a crew do if they find possible asbestos during construction cleaning?

Stop work in that area, keep people out and notify the GC. Only an inspection and, if needed, a licensed abatement contractor should handle it.

Is asbestos still found in commercial buildings?

Yes, in many buildings built before the 1980s, in flooring, mastic, pipe insulation, fireproofing and ceiling materials.

Asbestos abatement →

Can a cleaning company remove asbestos?

No. Asbestos removal requires licensed abatement contractors, trained workers, containment and air monitoring.

Asbestos abatement →

Is clearance testing required after asbestos abatement?

Clearance air testing is commonly required before the area can be reoccupied, depending on the project and jurisdiction.

Who can remove lead paint from a building?

EPA-certified renovators for renovation work and certified abatement contractors for abatement. Requirements depend on the building and type of work.

Why is lead dust dangerous?

Lead is toxic, and fine dust from old paint is easily ingested or inhaled. Children are especially vulnerable.

How is lead dust cleaned up after renovation?

With HEPA vacuuming and wet wiping in a defined sequence, followed by cleaning verification or clearance testing.

Leave them in place, keep people away and notify the supervisor. Trained personnel remove them with tools into approved sharps containers.

With exclusion measures such as netting, spikes and sealing openings, installed by pest control professionals.

What is the difference between cleaning and disinfecting?

Cleaning removes soil and residue; disinfecting kills specified microorganisms with a registered product used per label. Cleaning must come first.

Disinfection service with registered products →

Why does the disinfectant label matter?

The label sets the dilution, contact time and surfaces. Using it any other way may not work and may not be lawful.

Disinfection service with registered products →

What is contact time?

How long a disinfectant must stay wet on a surface to kill the microorganisms listed on its label.

Disinfection service with registered products →

Does a new building need disinfecting before opening?

Usually cleaning is enough. Healthcare, food and childcare spaces may add disinfection or sanitizing per their requirements.

Cleanup and restoration after storms, floods and similar events, from debris removal and drying to cleaning for reoccupancy.

How soon should storm restoration start?

As soon as the building is safe to enter. Drying within the first days limits mold and further damage.

Yes. Floodwater can carry sewage, chemicals and debris, so crews use protective equipment and contaminated materials are removed.
